result.title: Do Motion Tokenizers for Co-Speech Gesture Generation Encode Gesture Semantics?
result.summary: Discrete motion tokenizers encode motion as atomic units and are widely used for co-speech gesture generation. It remains unclear which motion properties, especially those relevant to gesture semantics, are recoverable from these codebooks. We probe a reconstruction-trained codebook using 19 co-speech gesture descriptors spanning from raw motion to abstract communicative function. Results show that geometry and handedness are readily decodable from token embeddings, while motion category is only weakly decoded despite showing systematic differences in discrete code usage. This gap between reconstruction quality and descriptor decodability suggests that reconstruction objectives alone do not guarantee that gesture semantics are captured, and that evaluating codebooks on such properties can guide the design of more semantic motion tokenizers.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文用 19 个共语手势描述子探测重建训练得到的离散动作码本，发现几何与左右手属性可从 token 嵌入中解码，但动作类别的可解码性很弱，尽管 token 使用模式存在系统性差异。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「重建目标不等于语义被编码」的诊断思路可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态是否真正承载任务必要语义，以及如何用探针评估内部表示的语义含量；但对象为动作生成而非视觉推理，联系需较多核查。
